Prevention: Use clean planting material from credible sources (Certified nurseries, seed multipliers, RAB).
Crop rotation with crops other than cucurbits, tomatoes, etc. which favours the survival and multiplication of the virus.
Avoid establishing a new passion fruit plantation near the suspected diseased field or ochard.
Avoid intercropping passion fruit with alternative hosts such as cucurbits and tomato.
Adopt proper plant spacing (3 m between plant and 2 m between rows) to avoid overlapping of vines that promotes mechanical spread of the virus.
Practise good field hygiene by removal of weeds which may act as alternative hosts for virus vectors.
Regular pruning to regulate the crop canopy so that the vectors cannot be hidden inside.
Disinfect pruning tools using disinfectants such as heat, Sodium hypochlorite (Jik: 750 ml/15
Monitoring: Monitor (twice a week) for light and dark green mosaic pattern on leaves of plants in the nursery and in the field.
Look for the presence of the aphid vectors at least twice a week throughout the crop growing cycle.
During the growing cycle, check for the presence of woody and hardy fruits which even appear shapeless with small juice area.
Direct Control: Uproot and bury (50 cm deep) infected vines.
Control vectors using botanical pesticides such as hot pepper, neem oil, pyrethrum, etc.
